title: Demand Response Platform
sub: Autonomous demand-response operations for the grid control room
say: Every second, a power grid has to balance supply and demand. When it can't, the control room pays penalties, risks the frequency, or cuts customers off. This is the Demand Response Platform. It turns flexible demand into a grid resource, and runs it end to end.

title: Balancing the grid is getting harder
points: Deviations from schedule are charged under DSM regulations
Renewables swing by hundreds of megawatts in minutes
Transmission corridors congest in specific places
The last resort, load shedding, means blackouts
say: Deviations from schedule are charged under the DSM regulations. Renewables swing by hundreds of megawatts in minutes. Transmission lines congest in specific places. And the last resort, load shedding, means blackouts. Flexible consumers can solve all of this, if someone can call on them fast, in the right place, and prove what they delivered.

title: The live grid is the workspace
say: The Overview is a spatial workspace. The live grid fills the screen: substations, transmission corridors, every two-hundred-and-twenty kilovolt station, generation and flexible participants. The numbers an operator watches float above it: the grid's need, the flexibility available, what is dispatched, and what is actually being delivered.

title: A demand surge opens a DR event
say: Here, a demand surge in Bengaluru pushes the state into over-drawal. The platform detects it, forecasts where it is heading, and opens a demand-response event. On the right, it answers the four operator questions: what is happening, what is at risk, what happens next, and what the system intends to do, explained from situation to outcome.

title: Select it, and the camera flies there
say: Select anything, an alarm, a line, a participant, or the event itself, and the camera flies there. The affected corridors and participants light up, and a detail card sits right beside the object.

title: Optimised, checked, approved, dispatched
say: The optimiser picks the cheapest reliable mix of batteries, flexible loads and generation, within network limits, in milliseconds. A digital twin checks every action first. Inside its autonomy envelope the platform acts on its own. Larger moves wait for the operator, with dual authorisation above two hundred megawatts. Then signed commands go out, and delivery responds live on the map.

title: Every event, fully accountable
say: Every event keeps its own record: target, dispatched and delivered over time, performance against baseline, the participants, the options that were considered, the safety checks, and a live activity log.

title: Flexibility, organised by programme
say: Programmes organise the flexibility: interruptible load, industrial curtailment, load shifting, distributed energy and electric vehicles, batteries, and supply-side flex. Choose one, and its participants light up on the map, with availability, reliability and price at a glance.

title: Scrub through any event
say: Any event can be replayed. Scrub the timeline, and the map shows exactly who was dispatched, when they acknowledged, and what they delivered.

title: Measured, paid, and on the record
say: When an event closes, delivery is measured against each participant's baseline, payments are adjusted for performance, reliability is learned for next time, and every step is written to a tamper-evident, hash-chained audit trail.

title: The last resort, under human control
say: And when flexibility is not enough? The platform proposes rotational load shedding, but only for the over-drawal that flexibility cannot cover, and never on its own. A shift-in-charge has to approve it.

title: Shared fairly, never on essential loads
say: Non-essential feeders are rostered fairly across the distribution companies. Spells are limited to forty-five minutes, and two hours a day. Hospitals, water works, railway traction and defence are never shed, and restoration is staged. Paid flexibility stays on, so shedding is always released first.

title: Every feeder, live on the map
say: Every two-hundred-and-twenty kilovolt feeder is live on the map. Shed areas turn red, and each station shows its roster group and the loads that stay protected.

title: Uncertainty you can see
say: Forecasts carry their uncertainty, predicted violations are flagged ahead of time, and data quality is checked continuously. When confidence drops, autonomy steps back to advisory on its own.

title: Autonomy as policy
say: Autonomy is a policy, not a leap of faith: monitor, advisory, supervised, or autonomous, with a kill switch, role-based access, and full traceability.

title: Demand Response Platform
sub: Detect · Forecast · Decide · Dispatch · Verify · Settle — with the operator in control
say: Demand Response Platform. Detect, decide, dispatch and verify, with the operator always in control.
